Viewed through the Financial Stability Report lens, the statement’s hold on the policy rate and the slowing of Treasury redemptions are modestly supportive, but vulnerabilities remain elevated. The FSR highlights ongoing risks from commercial real estate, nonbank leverage/private credit, large money market fund footprints and short-term funding linkages, and banks’ unrealized losses on fixed-rate/HTM assets tied to uninsured-deposit sensitivity; it also flags inflation pressures as a financial-stability risk. Given tighter credit conditions (SLOOS), heightened uncertainty, and active monitoring of fiscal and geopolitical risks, the net tone is positive but more cautious than a purely macro read of “solid” growth would suggest. Therefore, modestly positive, tempered.
